items.text: Eyoub Mohammad Nabil, an Iraqi prisoner accused of espionage, was executed on Sunday, October 11, in Lakaan Prison in Rasht. The death sentence had been previously issued. The execution took place at Lakaan Prison in Rasht.

South Korea is considering expanding its naval mission to the Sea of Oman and sending a maritime patrol aircraft to the area. The plan aims to ensure shipping security. Its implementation is likely to be postponed until after the war with the Islamic Republic ends.

Manchester City fans have revived the tradition of using inflatable bananas after the club was convicted of financial violations. Imre Varadi, the former striker, sells inflatable bananas for 10 pounds each and has received thousands of orders. This occurred after Manchester City's victory over Liverpool.

Ahmad Aryaeinejad, representative of Malayer, said Abbas Araghchi's negotiations are without coordination with the system's defined path. He emphasized that Iran is the decision-maker regarding uranium delivery to Russia. Aryaeinejad also called for internal consensus before negotiations.
The unidentified person named Peyman Ghadiri was buried on 23 Mehr. He had been in a coma since January 9, 2026, due to a gunshot wound. He died after about 9 months.

Volker Beck called for the immediate expulsion of the Iranian ambassador following the conviction of two suspects for spying for the IRGC Quds Force in a Hamburg court. He described the trial as evidence of the Islamic Republic exporting terrorism to Germany. Beck emphasized that this verdict should not remain without political consequences.

Two suspects linked to the IRGC were sentenced to a total of 13 years in prison in Germany for planning terrorist attacks. The Hamburg High Court president stated that the Islamic Republic is trying to export its terrorism to Germany. This news received widespread coverage in German media.

The seventh meeting of the UN Convention on Biological Diversity heads started in Yerevan. Several presidents and international officials, including Masoud Pezeshkian and Antonio Guterres, are attending. Farzia Sabti, an Iran International reporter, provides more details.

Citizens have criticized the costs of government gatherings and allocation of resources to supporters of the Islamic Republic in messages to Iran International. These criticisms come amid rising inflation and economic difficulties for the people. More details were provided by Leila Saadati.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, rejected Trump's threat about using the 'mother of bombs.' He emphasized that the Islamic Republic will respond decisively to any action against national interests and security. The armed forces are prepared to confront any mistaken action by the US.

A video shows that on Thursday night in Rasht, government-affiliated gatherings of so-called 'Janfada' forces continued. Some of these forces clashed with protesters who objected to the harassment and disturbance. This clash caused tension.

Danny Danon, Israel's ambassador to the UN, warned that the Islamic Republic, Hezbollah, and other regional groups might take actions such as missile drills, cyberattacks, or misinformation campaigns ahead of the Israeli elections. He stated that any attack would face devastating consequences. This warning was issued on Thursday, October 15.

A video shows female students in a school in Kermanshah singing the anthem "Nam-e Javid Vatan." They also chant the slogan "Long live the Shah, long live Iran." This video was received by Iran International.

Amir Mohammad Kohkan was killed by the forces of the Islamic Republic during the Iranian National Revolution on January 3, 2026. This event will remain in the memory of the Iranian people. His memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

Some Iran International viewers reported increased security measures in schools and the presence of individuals promoting against Prince Reza Pahlavi. Names of protesting students are recorded, and bags are searched in some schools. There are also reports of dress code enforcement, camera installation, audio recording, and body searches.

Nabih Berri, Speaker of the Lebanese Parliament, met with Saeed Khatibzadeh, Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister, to discuss developments in Lebanon and Tehran-Beirut relations. The meeting took place at the Parliament headquarters. Tofiq Samadi, Iran's chargé d'affaires in Lebanon, was also present.

Bank Keshavarzi has deducted the full salaries of all employees for October due to taxes and has not deposited any money. The reason given is to compensate for lower taxes paid in previous years. This issue has caused dissatisfaction among the employees.

A woman in Qom was sentenced to 50 lashes for kissing and hugging a man in a café. The sentence was issued based on her husband's complaint and a video of the physical interaction. The accused denied the charges.

Saeed Khatibzadeh, Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister, traveled to Lebanon. This trip coincided with intensified Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon and the seizure of a truck carrying explosives. It is possible that Khatibzadeh's meeting with Nabih Berri was aimed at manually transferring money to Hezbollah.

Ahmad Alamolhoda stated that diplomatic efforts in the war have reached a deadlock and failed. He said the enemy's military escalation is currently only a threat and has not reached the operational stage. Alamolhoda emphasized that the Islamic Republic must remain steadfast and not surrender or compromise.

Amir Mohammad Rostampour, Iran's 80 kg boxing representative, withdrew from the World Youth Boxing Championships after being matched against an Israeli opponent. The competition is held in Montenegro with over 500 athletes from 69 countries. The Iranian Boxing Federation explicitly stated that the withdrawal was due to refusal to fight the Israeli opponent.

Ali Shirazi stated that the IRGC held a drill to distribute 313,000 livelihood and dowry packages. These aids are not given to ordinary people but are reserved for supporters of the regime. The Islamic Republic aims to maintain the support of its backers amid economic pressure.

The nursing director of Mashhad University of Medical Sciences reported a shortage of about 2,500 nurses in the city. Hiring enough staff, improving salaries and benefits, and providing welfare facilities are essential to reduce nurse burnout. Nurses also face mandatory overtime, which increases their job stress.

Beth Dobbin, a 32-year-old British runner, has been diagnosed with ME disease and spends more than 22 hours a day in bed. Despite the risk of worsening her health, she agreed to an interview with BBC to raise public awareness about the disease. Her symptoms began after simultaneous infection with COVID-19 and glandular fever in winter 2021.

Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the summit of the 17th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity and in a meeting with the Prime Minister of Georgia, said the Islamic Republic is not seeking nuclear weapons and that destructive propaganda against Iran is a lie. He added that Iran has always been ready for dialogue but will not submit to force. Pezeshkian also called US sanctions and attacks in recent months unjustifiable and inhumane.

Alisina Mostafavi, a mountaineer and tar player, was executed on 22 Mehr 1405. A video showing his daughter mourning at his gravestone has been shared on social media. This news was reported by Iran International.

Saudi authorities released footage of attacks on Abha, Jazan, and Najran airports. The Saudi-led coalition reported that the attacks on Abha airport caused three deaths and 28 injuries. The coalition spokesperson stated that the Houthis attempted to target dozens of centers including airports.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported that 12 ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf, and the Sea of Oman in the past seven days. One ship sank and two ships were immobilized. Ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz remains about 70% lower than before the war started.

Naser Mohammadi, the temporary Friday prayer leader of Yazd, stated that the war must continue until lasting and reliable security is achieved. He considered negotiation with the US meaningless unless the US abandons its goals. He also said that prosecutors should act against the crime of improper hijab, but no action has been taken so far.
Zhina Ahmadi, a resident of Mariwan, has been detained in this city for 12 days. She remains in judicial uncertainty at the Sanandaj Correction and Rehabilitation Center. Her legal status is unclear.

Denmark criticized the actions of the Islamic Republic at the UN Security Council meeting. It called for an immediate halt to attacks against regional countries. Denmark also demanded the prevention of threats to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Persepolis women's football team secured their fourth consecutive win by defeating Palayesh Gaz Ilam 2-0. The goals were scored by Zahra Ghanbari and Mohaddeseh Zolfi. Persepolis remains at the top of the table and is preparing for the first women's football derby.

A kebab restaurant in the Sattarkhan neighborhood of Tehran was demolished due to customers not observing Islamic hijab. The incident involved police and municipal officers. The customer's voice in the video was reproduced using artificial intelligence for security reasons.

Mohammad Baqer Mohammadi Laeini, the Friday prayer leader of Sari, called those proposing a referendum or tactical retreat against the US traitors and internal mercenaries and demanded judicial action against them. He also criticized Turkey and Pakistan's support for Saudi Arabia under the Mecca Pact. The prayer leader stated that the Islamic Republic forces can target US submarines and predicted a major defeat for the US Navy soon.

The will of Majid Nikandish, a 25-year-old protester from Quchan who was arrested and executed during the December protests, has been published. In his letter, he asked for forgiveness from his family and expressed his fear of execution. His death sentence was carried out on October 8, 2026, in Mashhad.

Joachim Wadtfoll, Germany's foreign minister, stated that Europe is within the reach of the Islamic Republic and the German government will not tolerate Tehran's hostile activities. He referred to a Hamburg State Supreme Court ruling that revealed the Islamic Republic's role in an assassination attempt on two individuals. The foreign minister emphasized that they will respond to this matter.

Real Madrid has demanded the immediate resignation of Javier Tebas from the presidency of La Liga and vice-presidency of the Spanish Football Federation. This request came after Tebas compared Real Madrid's TV operations to the propaganda methods of Joseph Goebbels. The club described this comparison as intolerable and offensive.

Forough Kanani referred to the Hamburg court ruling against two agents linked to the IRGC. She said European countries are now seeing the consequences of their appeasement policy with the Islamic Republic. She also emphasized that Iranians abroad had warned for years about the threat of terrorist actions.

The commander of the Missing Persons Search Committee said that Qatar's explanations about the fate of the Iranian pilots were not convincing. A second team will be sent to Qatar to investigate the matter. The International Committee of the Red Cross is also following up on the issue.

The Esteghlal women's football team defeated Sepahan 2-1 in the fourth week of the Premier League. Both goals for Esteghlal were scored by Niloufar Azimi in the second half. Next week, Esteghlal and Persepolis will hold the first women's derby.

Tensions between the Islamic Republic of Iran and Lebanon have escalated due to Beirut's refusal to accept the credentials of the Tehran-appointed ambassador. Abbas Araghchi contacted Joseph Aoun, and Saeed Khatibzadeh traveled to Beirut. These developments have attracted attention.

Mohammad Bagherzadeh, commander of the Missing Persons Search Committee, said that the statements of Qatari officials about the status of Iranian pilots were not convincing. The issue is being pursued through the Ministry of Interior and the International Committee of the Red Cross. A second expert team has been dispatched to continue the investigations.

Hossein Mohammadi, temporary Friday prayer leader of Isfahan, said that the US neither intends to send ground troops to Iran nor has the capability to do so. He added that the Islamic Republic will not surrender to US pressures relying on its armed forces and people's support. Mohammadi also urged regional countries to cooperate instead of relying on US security support.

From April to October 1405, dozens of Baha'i citizens in Yazd faced house searches, confiscation of belongings, summons for interrogation, and judicial prosecution. A gathering of about 50 people was dispersed, and three citizens were sentenced to prison. Authorities confiscated mobile phones and personal items, some of which have not yet been returned.

The Tehran Fire Department reported a fire in the shopping and café area of the Enghelab Sports Complex. The incident occurred on the afternoon of Friday, October 16. The cause and any casualties have not yet been announced.

Police entered a high school in Saint-Denis, France, to arrest a teenager, causing protests from teachers and students. The third round of negotiations with the Minister of Education ended without agreement. Disputes over the October 17 demonstration in Paris continue.

A young Norwegian was sentenced to 20 years in prison for a murder conspiracy ordered by the Islamic Republic. In Germany, two agents linked to the IRGC were sentenced to a total of 13 years in prison. The trial of three Iranian nationals accused of espionage and planning attacks on Iran International journalists in London continues.

Donald Trump stated that he does not intend to send ground troops to Iran or use nuclear weapons against the Islamic Republic. He also said the US is negotiating with Russia and China about nuclear disarmament. These remarks were made in an interview with Newsmax.

During the suppression of the national revolution in Semnan province, government forces deployed snipers and armed agents in religious sites and student centers. These forces were present in the office of the Friday prayer leader, student dormitories, and the broadcasting organization. The purpose of this deployment was to shoot at protesting people.

Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel has eliminated Yahya Sinwar and other leaders of Hamas and Hezbollah through continued military operations. He said that if the war had stopped, Sinwar would not have been killed. Netanyahu attributed the killing of these leaders to the advance in Rafah and control of the Gaza border area.

The Malavan women's football team defeated Avaye Tehran 2-1 in the fourth week of the Iranian women's premier league. This was Malavan's first victory of the season, with Yasna Jafarzadeh scoring the team's first goal from a free kick. Before this match, Malavan had not scored any goals.

Seyed Ahmad Mostafanejad, a citizen from Piranshahr, was arrested after being summoned by the IRGC intelligence in the city. He was transferred to an unknown location. This event occurred on Wednesday, October 14.

Amir Mohammad Rostampour withdrew from the World Youth Boxing Championships due to refusing to fight an Israeli opponent. He has two bronze medals in Asian age group championships. The Iranian Boxing Federation announced this matter.

Armed Hezbollah members besieged an Iranian drug warehouse in Beirut on Friday, October 16. This occurred during security forces' attempt to seize spoiled drugs. After the army reinforcements arrived, the armed Hezbollah members withdrew.

The International Maritime Organization reported 113 maritime incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and the Middle East as of October 14. The mine clearance operation in the Strait of Hormuz has not yet been carried out and will resume after the conflicts end. The organization is also involved in negotiations to resume ship traffic.

Electric vehicle sales in Canada have increased by 55 percent. The share of fully electric models has reached seven percent of the market. Experts say this growth is not enough to achieve the 75 percent target by 2035.
A fuel carrier died following gunfire by military forces in the Iranshahr area. A fuel carrier's vehicle overturned due to the shooting. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Javidnam Ahmadi Khosravani, a 21-year-old basketball player and student at Sharif University of Technology, was shot dead on the evening of Thursday, January 8, 2026. His sister posted a video expressing her longing for her brother and family and lamented the denial of the right to mourn. Ahmadi Khosravani was the top player in the Tehran basketball league in 2025.

Less than three weeks remain until the US midterm elections, with intense competition between Republicans and Democrats for control of Congress. Economy, living costs, and the war with the Islamic Republic are the main concerns of voters. The election results could affect Donald Trump's power in the remaining two years of his presidency.

Ali Kayali, a commander allied with Bashar al-Assad and the main suspect in the killing of 248 civilians in Syria, was abducted near Beirut by Syrian and Turkish intelligence agents and transferred to Syria. The operation was reportedly coordinated with Lebanese authorities, but a Lebanese security official denied their knowledge. The official Syrian news agency confirmed Kayali's arrest.

Elon Musk unveiled the new version of the Tesla Roadster after nearly 9 years of waiting at the SpaceX test site. The car accelerates from zero to 100 km/h in less than one second and can lift off the ground using compressed air engines. Official production of this joint Tesla and SpaceX product will begin in 2028.

In the past week, reports of environmental crises in Iran were published. These included the death of a female bear, discovery of four Caspian seal carcasses, air pollution in several cities, and forest fires. Arrests of suspects involved in illegal hunting and natural resource trafficking were also reported.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry, denied any Iranian involvement in the Houthi military operations. He stated that Yemeni armed forces act based on their own interests and Iran is ready to help peacefully resolve the conflicts. He also called for an end to foreign intervention and the blockade of Yemen.

Amir Ghalenoei stated that there has been a youth movement in the Iranian national football team, with players like Aria Yousefi, Hardani, Rezaqinia, and Mahmoudi added to the team. He criticized the team's difficulties in playing matches during the FIFA dates and said the upcoming FIFA date will help the team. He also rejected conditions for winning the Asian Cup and contract extensions, expressing gratitude to the football federation.

Donald Trump said the issue of normalizing relations between Israel and Saudi Arabia within the Abraham Accords has been raised again. He expressed a positive view on Saudi Arabia joining these accords. Trump also expressed confidence about Israel's assistance to Saudi Arabia in confronting the Houthis.

Brad Cooper, CENTCOM commander, stated that US actions have blocked $25 billion of Iranian oil exports and increased economic pressure on the Islamic Republic and the IRGC. CENTCOM also helped block nearly $350 million in cryptocurrency assets linked to Iran. The pressures have affected Iran's ability to pay salaries to employees and paramilitary forces.

In two separate incidents in Urmia and Mashhad, two workers died and one was injured. These incidents occurred in a water well in Urmia and a charcoal production workshop in Mashhad. More details were published by Harana News Agency.

Zelensky smiled and said, "That is my answer," in response to a Sky News reporter's question about Trump using him as a scapegoat. This reaction was met with laughter from those present at the press conference.

Alaeddin Boroujerdi responded to Donald Trump's remarks about the possible use of the so-called 'mother of bombs' against Iran by saying the Islamic Republic will use the 'father of missiles.' He emphasized that Iran's policy regarding the Strait of Hormuz will not change and that it will be maintained with strength. Boroujerdi urged Trump to refrain from threatening the Islamic Republic.

A container ship flying the Singapore flag sank in the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by a projectile from the IRGC and catching fire. Videos show boxes of iPhones, perfume, and shoes floating on the water, with people collecting these items by boat. This report is based on an interview with Farnaz Davari, a member of the Iran International editorial team.

For the first time in Iranian women's football, the VAR system was used during the Kerman derby between Khatoon Bam and Gol Gohar Sirjan. The match ended in a goalless draw. Mahnaz Zakaei and Atena Lashani were the VAR referees.

Saeed Khatibzadeh stated that Tehran is ready to engage with Washington if the US seeks a balanced agreement based on mutual respect. He emphasized that the US should not expect to gain anything in negotiations that it could not achieve in war. He also highlighted diplomatic resolution of disputes and respect for Iran's rights.

A man was killed in Tehran during a dispute motivated by honor. The suspect, who initially fled, was identified and arrested by police in Malayer County. This incident was reported by Harana News Agency.

Executions of two prisoners were carried out in Yazd and Gorgan prisons. The number of executed prisoners in Adel Abad prison in Shiraz reached two. Additionally, one death row prisoner in Ahvaz was spared after the victim's family pardoned him.

Mehdi Nakhl Ahmadi said the emphasis of Friday prayer leaders on continuing the war with the US reflects a faction of the government worried about a power shift if an agreement is reached. He added that despite economic pressures on people, the ruling faction insists on resistance and suppresses opposing voices. Figures like Khatami and Rouhani face efforts by the ruling faction to marginalize their views.
Elnaz Ghorbani, a Christian convert, was summoned to serve her five-year prison sentence after receiving a notification.

Donald Trump, the US president, said at a campaign rally in Dalton, Georgia, that the war with the Islamic Republic will end 'very, very soon' and stressed that Iran will never obtain a nuclear weapon. He noted that before the military operations, the US economy was in very good condition. Trump added that he was compelled to act to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons.

On the evening of October 16, two missiles struck Aden International Airport in Yemen. Passengers of a plane were evacuated to Cairo while another plane was en route to Aden. Aden police identified Iran-backed Houthis as responsible for the attack.

Brad Cooper stated that US actions have so far prevented the export of at least 25 billion dollars of Iranian crude oil. Nearly 350 million dollars in cryptocurrency assets related to the Islamic Republic have also been blocked. Economic pressures have affected the Islamic Republic's ability to pay security forces' salaries.

Kambiz Tavana stated that the US military presence in the region is not only for military operations but also to exert economic pressure and limit the financial resources of the Islamic Republic. He added that Trump's remarks about the imminent end of the war may be based on assessments of the impact of sanctions. The US is considering continuing economic pressure without escalating military operations.

The UK Foreign Office has advised its citizens to avoid non-essential travel to Saudi Arabia. This warning covers the entire country except for areas with a higher alert. It also recommends avoiding King Khalid International Airport until its security is assured.

A shipment containing 780 kilograms of C-4 and TNT explosives was seized last week in Lebanon. The explosives were intended for use in explosive drones against Israeli forces. The seizure highlights the dispute between Hezbollah and the Lebanese government over disarmament.

Benjamin Netanyahu warned that any attack by the Islamic Republic of Iran on Israel would be a big mistake. He said Israel can attack Iran alone or with the United States. Netanyahu emphasized that there is no option other than overthrowing the Islamic Republic in Iran.

An airstrike targeted Houthi forces supported by the Islamic Republic in the village of Al-Azlah west of Taiz, Yemen. No details about the attacker or casualties were released. Fighting in Taiz province has intensified, causing widespread displacement of civilians.

The White House announced that Donald Trump issued an executive order suspending part of the sanctions and tariffs under the Russia and Iran sanctions law. This decision was made two days before the new regulations were to take effect. Trump deemed the exemption in the national interest of the United States and notified Congress.

The IRGC Navy announced that a supertanker carrying over two million barrels of crude oil struck a naval mine and caught fire while passing through the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC claims the tanker had its navigation and radar systems turned off and attempted to pass with US support. The Strait of Hormuz has been declared closed, and warnings were issued to follow the passage regulations.

Israel's Kan TV reported that Israel, mediated by the US, has begun sharing security intelligence about the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen with Saudi Arabia. According to the report, Saudi Arabia requested assistance from the US, and Washington relayed this request to Israel. The primary goal of this cooperation is stated to be securing navigation in the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

Based on data from the Statistical Center, the annual housing cost for urban households in Iran rose from about 7.8 million tomans in 2014 to over 117 million tomans in 2024. Tehran was the most expensive province in the country during this period.

Hooshang Hassanyari, a Middle East expert, said China can play a greater role in ensuring security in the Persian Gulf due to its dependence on the region's energy. He emphasized that China currently benefits from US military spending for shipping security without taking proportional responsibility.

Shahram Khaldi, a researcher of Middle Eastern history and international relations, said the Islamic Republic is counting on levers including the geographical position of the Strait of Hormuz, the reconstruction of missile and drone capabilities, proxy forces, and internal repression against US military and economic pressures. According to Khaldi, Tehran is trying to influence the timing of potential US attacks by using the strategic position of the Strait of Hormuz.

Miad Maleki said Trump's new decision on Russia sanctions does not create a new opportunity for Iran to bypass sanctions. He emphasized that Russia seeks its own interests and cannot help Tehran. The halt of Iran's oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz has benefited Russia.

A court in the UK convicted a 19-year-old Norwegian of conspiracy to commit murder on behalf of a criminal network linked to the Islamic Republic. He was sentenced to 20 years in prison. The report was published by Golareh Han from Iran International.

EU leaders emphasized continuing pressure on Moscow at the Brussels meeting. Ursula von der Leyen announced preparations for the 22nd sanctions package. Volodymyr Zelensky requested 70 billion euros in aid for the next year.

Omid Memarian said that the US goal is not only to destroy Iran's military and nuclear facilities. Washington wants to change the Islamic Republic officials' calculation about the cost of continuing resistance. The US tries to convey that resistance is possible but may come at the cost of the Islamic Republic's destruction.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the Islamic Republic of Iran has increased its military, intelligence, and operational support to the Houthis. This support includes providing security information, military training, and assistance in targeting missile and drone attacks. The presence of IRGC officers on the front lines has also been reported.

Mohammad Taghavi analyzed the match between Zob Ahan and Sepahan, stating that despite over two decades of professional football in Iran, childish mistakes still occur in matches. This indicates that there is still a long way to go for full professionalism.

Majid Ibn al-Reza, the acting head of Iran's Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics, reacted to recent statements by Donald Trump about the use of "the mother of all bombs," saying that the Islamic Republic's missile power has changed the equations. He wrote on his social media that the titles and dimensions of bombs are not important, and America's bombs will explode in its global reputation, economy, and electoral equations. Ibn al-Reza added that Iran's missile power has changed the equations.

The 40th-day memorial ceremony of Erfan Mirzaei was held in the village of Gharghan, Isfahan province. The circumstances of the death of this 21-year-old rapper are unclear, with some sources reporting his execution. Two sources told Iran International that he died due to severe torture in Isfahan's Dastgerd prison.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated at the inauguration ceremony of educational projects that every capable person can take on greater responsibilities. He emphasized that managers should not hinder the talents of others and that education is a right for all children. He also stressed the need to improve education quality and transform teaching methods.

A minibus carrying workers from the Mahabad sugar factory collided with a Nissan pickup on the Mahabad to Miandoab road. One worker died and 12 others were injured in the accident. The incident resulted in casualties and injuries.

Hossein Aghaei said the Islamic Republic is trying to increase the cost of confrontation for the US and Israel by continuing attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. He added that economic pressure limits Tehran's ability to sustain these attacks. There is also uncertainty about Donald Trump's strategy towards the Islamic Republic.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin from Iran International says Israel and Saudi Arabia are exchanging security information to counter the Houthis. He emphasizes that the Islamic Republic has invested for over a decade to strengthen the Houthis' military capabilities. This cooperation is part of a broader regional collaboration that goes beyond Yemen.
Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, paid respects at the statue of Qasem Soleimani and Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis.

Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, arrived in Baghdad to attend the meeting of foreign ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation. The chairmanship of the organization will be transferred from Turkey to Iraq during this meeting. Hakan Fidan, Turkey's foreign minister, is also attending the meeting.
